speaker: Doctor
text:
I see you're experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To better understand your condition, can you tell me if these symptoms worsened after a recent viral illness or trauma?

REQUEST TEST: Thyroid_Stimulating_Hormone (TSH), Creatine_Kinase (CK), and Antinuclear Antibodies (ANA).

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information; given the symmetrical weakness and lack of viral triggers, I need to rule out myasthenia gravis and metabolic causes. REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine Receptor Antibodies (AChR-Ab) and Repetitive Nerve Stimulation. Please let me know if your double vision improves when you close one eye or rest.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies: Present (elevated); Repetitive_Nerve_Stimulation: Decreased muscle response with repetitive stimulation
